Passage (Chinese)

当时，有几个文士和法利赛人对耶稣说：“夫子，我们愿意你显个神迹给我们看。”耶稣回答说：“一个邪恶淫乱的世代求看神迹，除了先知约拿的神迹以外，再没有神迹给他们看。”


Passage (English, ESV)

Then some of the scribes and Pharisees said to him, “Teacher, we wish to see a sign from you.” But he answered them, “An evil and adulterous generation seeks for a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.”


Passage (English, NLT)

Some teachers of religious law and Pharisees came and said to him, "Teacher, we want to see a miraculous sign from you." He replied, "You evil people! You demand a miraculous sign, but none will be given to you except the sign of Jonah."


Context & Short Commentary

This exchange (Matthew 12:38-39 / parallels in Mark and Luke) captures a recurring theme: religious leaders demand spectacular proof, but Jesus emphasizes faith and points to the only sign that will be given — the sign of Jonah (his death, burial, and resurrection). The phrase “an evil and adulterous generation” is a strong rebuke; it highlights spiritual unfaithfulness rather than mere curiosity.

Key points:

• The request comes from scribes and Pharisees — religious insiders whose motive is often testing rather than genuine seeking.
• Jesus reframes the debate: signs are not a substitute for repentance and trust.
• The "sign of Jonah" prefigures Jesus' own resurrection and invites deeper reflection on repentance and new life.
Questions for Group Study

1. What do you think motivated the scribes and Pharisees to ask for a sign? Was there any constructive basis for their request?
2. How does Jesus' response change the focus of the conversation from display to heart condition?
3. What does the "sign of Jonah" mean in this passage and how should it shape our understanding of Jesus' mission?
4. Can we identify modern examples where people look for signs instead of wrestling with faith and repentance?
Short Reflection Exercise (5–10 minutes)

• Read the passage silently. Then write one sentence: What is God inviting you to believe or change after reading this?
